examples.ko: 새로 온 직원이 팀에 빨리 융화했어요.
examples.en: The new employee blended into the team quickly.
Different cultures blend together naturally.

examples.ko: 처음에는 낯설었지만 지금은 동네 사람들과 잘 융화하고 있어요.
examples.en: It felt strange at first, but now I get along well with the people in the neighborhood.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 융화하지 못해서 합병이 어려웠어요.
examples.en: The merger was difficult because the two companies couldn't come together.

examples.ko: 여러 나라 출신 학생들이 한 반에서 융화하며 지내요.
examples.en: Students from many countries get along in one class.
I tried hard to fit in with my new family.

explain: '어울리다'는 일상에서 두루 쓰지만, '융화하다'는 서로 다른 사람이나 문화, 집단이 하나처럼 섞일 때 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 써요. 보통 '~와/과 융화하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '어울리다' is the everyday word, while '융화하다' is used in writing and news when different people, cultures or groups blend into one. It is usually used as '~와/과 융화하다'.

examples.ko: 윷놀이는 윷가락 네 개를 던져서 해요.
examples.en: You play yutnori by throwing four yut sticks.
I threw the yut sticks and got a mo.
These are yut sticks my grandfather made himself.
One of the yut sticks rolled out of the room.

examples.ko: 설날에 가족이 모여 윷가락 던지는 소리가 방 안에 가득했어요.
examples.en: On Lunar New Year, the sound of the family throwing yut sticks filled the room.

examples.ko: 윷가락이 어디 갔는지 같이 찾아 주세요.
examples.en: Please help me look for where the yut sticks went.

explain: 윷놀이에서 던지는 막대 네 개를 가리켜요. 놀이 이름은 '윷놀이'이고, 설날 같은 명절에 가족끼리 많이 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the four sticks you throw in yutnori. The game itself is called '윷놀이', and families often play it on holidays such as Lunar New Year.

examples.en: I was so angry that I ground my teeth.
I crunched down on a hard candy.

examples.ko: 얼음을 으드득 씹어 먹으면 이에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Crunching on ice is bad for your teeth.

examples.ko: 자는 동안 으드득 소리가 나서 잠에서 깼어요.
examples.en: A grinding sound woke me up while I was sleeping.

examples.ko: 으드득 소리가 날 만큼 세게 깨물었어요.
examples.en: I bit down so hard that it made a crunching sound.

examples.ko: 그는 으드득 소리를 내며 이를 악물었어요.
examples.en: He clenched his teeth with a grinding sound.

explain: 단단한 것을 힘주어 깨물거나 이를 갈 때 나는 소리를 흉내 내는 말이에요. 눈을 밟는 소리는 보통 '뽀드득'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound of biting hard on something firm or grinding your teeth. The sound of stepping on snow is usually '뽀드득' instead.

examples.en: The boss threatened us to finish it by today.
The older brother made a threat to his younger brother.

examples.ko: 아무리 으름장을 놓아도 아이는 겁먹지 않았어요.
examples.en: No matter how much I threatened him, the child wasn't scared.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 으름장 때문에 모두 입을 다물었어요.
examples.en: Everyone kept quiet because of his threats.

examples.ko: 으름장만 놓고 실제로 한 건 없어요.
examples.en: He only makes threats and has never actually done anything.

examples.ko: 빨리 안 나가면 혼난다는 으름장에 아이들이 도망갔어요.
examples.en: The kids ran away at the warning that they'd be in trouble if they didn't leave.

explain: 보통 '으름장을 놓다'로 써요. 말로 겁을 줘서 상대가 뜻대로 하게 하려는 느낌이고, '협박'보다 가볍게 들릴 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '으름장을 놓다'. It means scaring someone with words to make them do what you want, and it often sounds lighter than '협박' (a serious threat).

examples.en: My friend's house was so grand that I was surprised.
The hotel lobby is really magnificent.

examples.ko: 으리으리한 저택이 언덕 위에 서 있어요.
examples.en: A grand mansion stands on top of the hill.

examples.ko: 시내에 으리으리하게 지은 건물이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A lavishly built building has opened downtown.
The wedding hall was so lavish that it felt a bit overwhelming.

examples.ko: 건물이 으리으리하다고 해서 다 좋은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because a building is grand doesn't mean it's all good.

explain: 크고 화려한 집이나 건물을 보고 감탄할 때 주로 써요. '웅장하다'보다 말투가 편하고 감탄하는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used when you are impressed by a big, showy house or building. It sounds more casual than '웅장하다' and carries a stronger feeling of amazement.

examples.en: I put the snacks in my bag and they ended up crushed.
Dry leaves crumble under my feet.
The cookie was crushed and only crumbs were left.
I gripped it hard and the paper cup in my hand got crushed.
I sprinkle crushed cookies over ice cream.

examples.ko: 상자가 눌려서 안에 있는 빵이 다 으스러질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The box got squashed and the bread inside almost got completely crushed.

explain: '부서지다'와 비슷하지만 눌리거나 짓눌려서 잘게 깨지는 느낌이 있어요. 힘을 주는 쪽에서 말할 때는 '으스러뜨리다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '부서지다' but suggests something breaking into small pieces from being pressed or squashed. When you focus on the one applying force, the word is '으스러뜨리다'.

examples.ko: 복도 형광등이 오래돼서 밤이 되면 어둡고 으스스해요.
examples.en: The hallway lights are old, so it gets dark and eerie at night.
The atmosphere was eerie when I went into the empty house.

examples.ko: 비를 맞았더니 몸이 으스스하고 열이 나는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I got rained on, and I feel chilly and think I have a fever.

examples.ko: 으스스한 이야기를 들었더니 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I heard a creepy story and now I can't sleep.

examples.ko: 안개 낀 새벽에는 공원이 으스스하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: The park feels eerie in the foggy early morning.
It's chilly in the mornings and evenings, so I brought a jacket.

explain: 무서워서 소름이 돋는 분위기와, 추워서 몸이 떨리는 느낌 두 가지에 써요. 몸이 으슬으슬한 느낌은 '으슬으슬'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It covers two feelings: a creepy atmosphere that gives you goosebumps, and a cold shiver in the body. For a body shiver, '으슬으슬' is also commonly used.

examples.en: I feel chilly, maybe because I'm coming down with a cold.
I got rained on, and my body is shivering with chills.
I felt a chill, so I pulled the blanket over me.
I've had chills since this morning. Should I go to the doctor?
When evening came, I got chills and goosebumps.
Warm ginger tea is good when you have the chills.

explain: 열이 나려고 하거나 비를 맞은 뒤처럼 몸이 오싹오싹 추운 느낌에 써요. 날씨 자체보다 몸 상태 때문에 한기가 들 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes shivery chills in the body, like when a fever is coming on or after getting rained on. It fits best when the chill comes from your body's condition rather than just the weather.

examples.en: After getting praised, he puffed up his shoulders proudly.
My younger sibling is swaggering after getting first place on the exam.
He walked proudly in his new shoes.
If you show off too much, your friends won't like it.
It was cute how he swelled with pride at a single compliment.

examples.ko: 상을 받았다고 그렇게 으쓱거릴 것까지는 없어요.
examples.en: You don't need to swagger like that just because you won a prize.

explain: 우쭐해서 뽐내듯 어깨를 들썩이는 모습에 써요. 모르겠다는 뜻으로 어깨를 올리는 동작은 보통 '어깨를 으쓱하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes swaggering with your shoulders raised out of pride. The gesture of raising your shoulders to say 'I don't know' is usually '어깨를 으쓱하다'.

examples.ko: 아이를 윽박지르지 말고 차분히 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't bully the child; talk calmly.

examples.ko: 상사가 부하 직원을 윽박질러서 분위기가 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: The boss browbeat his staff and the mood turned bad.

examples.ko: 큰 소리로 윽박질러도 문제는 해결되지 않아요.
examples.en: Even if you yell and bully, the problem won't be solved.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말이 안 통하면 윽박지르기부터 해요.
examples.en: When he can't get through to someone, he starts by browbeating them.

examples.ko: 가게 주인이 손님한테 윽박지르는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the shop owner bullying a customer.

examples.ko: 윽박지른다고 해서 사람이 마음을 바꾸지는 않아요.
examples.en: Bullying someone doesn't make them change their mind.

explain: '혼내다'와 달리 큰 소리나 힘으로 상대를 눌러서 말을 못 하게 하는 느낌이에요. '르' 불규칙이라 '윽박질러요'가 되고, 재촉하며 몰아붙일 때는 '다그치다'도 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '혼내다' (to scold), it suggests overpowering someone with a loud voice or force so they can't speak back. It is a '르' irregular verb, so it becomes '윽박질러요'. For pressing someone hard to hurry, '다그치다' is also used.

examples.ko: 그 화가는 산속에 은거해서 그림만 그렸어요.
examples.en: That painter lived in seclusion in the mountains and only painted.

examples.ko: 은퇴한 뒤 시골에 은거하며 살고 있어요.
examples.en: After retiring, he lives a secluded life in the countryside.
The king left the palace and lived in seclusion at a temple.

examples.ko: 그는 오랫동안 세상과 담을 쌓고 은거했어요.
examples.en: He cut himself off from the world and lived in seclusion for a long time.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 은거하는 동안 소설 세 편을 썼어요.
examples.en: That author wrote three novels while living in seclusion.

examples.ko: 가끔은 아무도 없는 곳에 은거하고 싶어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I want to retreat to a place where no one is around.

explain: 세상일에서 물러나 조용히 숨어 사는 것을 말하는데, 글이나 역사 이야기, 뉴스에서 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '시골에 내려가 조용히 산다'처럼 말하는 게 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means withdrawing from worldly affairs to live quietly in hiding, and you will see it in writing, history stories and news. In everyday talk, something like '시골에 내려가 조용히 산다' (moving to the countryside and living quietly) sounds more natural.

examples.en: He is a hermit who lives avoiding people.
There's a rumor that a hermit lives in the mountains.

examples.ko: 그는 은둔자처럼 집에서 거의 나오지 않았어요.
examples.en: He hardly ever left his house, like a hermit.
The main character of this novel appears as a hermit.

examples.ko: 그 작가가 은둔자로 살게 된 이유가 궁금해요.
examples.en: I'm curious why that writer came to live as a recluse.
A hermit's life looks lonely.

explain: '집순이·집돌이'는 집에 있는 걸 좋아하는 가벼운 말이고, '은둔자'는 사람들을 일부러 피해 지내는 무거운 느낌이에요. 뉴스에서는 '은둔형 외톨이'라는 말도 나와요.
explain_en: '집순이/집돌이' is a light word for someone who likes staying home, while '은둔자' has a heavier feel of deliberately avoiding people. In the news you will also see '은둔형 외톨이' (a socially withdrawn person).

examples.ko: 은연중에 아버지의 말투를 따라 하게 돼요.
examples.en: I find myself unconsciously copying my father's way of speaking.
He let his true feelings show without meaning to.

examples.ko: 은연중에 한 말이 친구에게 상처가 됐나 봐요.
examples.en: I think something I said without thinking hurt my friend.

examples.ko: 광고는 은연중에 우리 생각에 영향을 줘요.
examples.en: Ads subtly influence our thinking without us noticing.

examples.ko: 저도 은연중에 그 사람을 의식하고 있었어요.
examples.en: I was subconsciously aware of that person too.
Nothing was said, but you can sense it all indirectly.

explain: 거의 '은연중에' 꼴로 써요. 자기도 모르게, 또는 겉으로 드러내지 않은 채 마음이나 뜻이 슬쩍 드러나는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '은연중에'. It carries the feel of a thought or intention slipping out without you realizing it, or without being openly stated.

examples.en: This poem has many metaphorical expressions.
You have to understand that remark metaphorically.
The author criticized society in a metaphorical way.
The title of that novel is metaphorical.
The more metaphorical something is, the more its interpretations differ.
This painting is metaphorical, so it needs an explanation.

explain: '은유적인 표현', '은유적으로'처럼 써요. '직접적'의 반대쪽에 있고, '비유적'과 가까운 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used as '은유적인 표현' or '은유적으로'. It sits opposite '직접적' (direct) and is close in meaning to '비유적' (figurative).

examples.ko: 방 안에 향초 냄새가 은은히 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: The scent of the candle spread softly through the room.
A bell can be heard faintly in the distance.
The moonlight shines gently on the lake.

examples.ko: 그 꽃은 은은히 좋은 향이 나요.
examples.en: That flower has a soft, pleasant fragrance.
Her softly smiling face was really pretty.

examples.ko: 은은히 켜 둔 조명 덕분에 분위기가 좋아요.
examples.en: Thanks to the softly lit lights, the mood is nice.

explain: 소리, 빛, 향기가 뚜렷하지 않고 부드럽게 느껴질 때 써요. 형용사 '은은하다'는 '은은한 향기'처럼 꾸며 주는 말로 쓰고, 좋은 느낌으로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when a sound, light or scent isn't strong but is felt softly. The adjective '은은하다' is used as in '은은한 향기' (a subtle fragrance), and it usually has a positive feel.

examples.en: The rainy winter weather is dreary.
The closed market had a bleak atmosphere.
It was an evening with a dismal wind blowing.

examples.ko: 사람 없는 빈 거리가 을씨년스럽게 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: The empty street with no people felt desolate.
The day is cloudy and gloomy, so I don't want to go out.
The ruined factory looked bleak.

explain: 날씨나 풍경이 쓸쓸하고 우중충할 때 써요. '으스스하다'는 오싹하거나 추운 느낌이 중심이고, '을씨년스럽다'는 쓸쓸하고 가라앉은 느낌이 중심이에요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '을씨년스러워요'가 돼요.
explain_en: It describes weather or scenery that feels lonely and dreary. '으스스하다' centers on a creepy or chilly feeling, while '을씨년스럽다' centers on a desolate, gloomy mood. It is a 'ㅂ' irregular adjective, so it becomes '을씨년스러워요'.

examples.en: He recites a poem in a low voice.
Grandmother did the laundry humming a song under her breath.

examples.ko: 버스 안에서 가사를 읊조리는 사람이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was someone murmuring song lyrics on the bus.
The child softly recited a prayer and then fell asleep.
She murmured to herself as if talking alone, looking out the window.
Try speaking slowly, as if reciting a poem.

explain: 큰 소리로 외치는 게 아니라 낮은 목소리로 혼자 시나 노래, 말을 느낌 있게 입 밖에 낼 때 써요. '중얼거리다'는 불분명하게 혼자 말하는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is not for shouting; it means saying a poem, song or words in a low voice, to yourself and with feeling. '중얼거리다' leans more toward mumbling something unclear.

examples.en: The melody of that song is beautiful.
I danced slowly to the melody.

examples.ko: 어디선가 아름다운 음률을 타고 노랫소리가 들렸어요.
examples.en: From somewhere, singing drifted in on a beautiful melody.
Listening to the melody of the gayageum calms my mind.

examples.ko: 시도 음률로 읽으면 더 쉽게 외워져요.
examples.en: A poem is easier to memorize if you read it with a rhythm.
It's a song where the melody and lyrics go well together.

explain: '멜로디'가 더 편한 말이고, '음률'은 글에서 쓰는 듯한 느낌이 나요. 노래나 악기 소리의 가락뿐 아니라 시를 읽을 때 느껴지는 가락에도 써요.
explain_en: '멜로디' is the more casual word, while '음률' has a written, literary feel. It is used for the tune of songs and instruments, and also for the rhythm you feel when reading a poem.
